featured.title: Middle East Energy Crisis Sends Oil Higher
featured.content: Global oil prices have risen sharply as fresh attacks around Saudi Arabia and the Strait of Hormuz increase fears that disruption to Middle Eastern energy supplies could last for an extended period. Brent crude climbed above $107 a barrel in the latest trading, while Saudi Arabia continues to deal with the disruption of its East-West oil pipeline. At the same time, Houthi forces in Yemen are putting pressure on the Bab el-Mandeb route. The combination of threats to two major maritime corridors is increasing concerns about fuel prices, inflation and the wider global economy.

articles.title: 🚨 Oil Prices Rise as Middle East Supply Risks Intensify
articles.description: Global oil prices have moved higher after fresh attacks around Saudi Arabia and the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.content: Brent crude rose to around $107 a barrel as traders assessed the possibility of prolonged disruption to Middle Eastern energy supplies. The latest increase follows attacks affecting Saudi infrastructure and shipping around the Strait of Hormuz. The market is also watching the situation in Yemen, where Houthi forces have strengthened their position around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
articles.imageQuery: Brent crude oil market tanker Middle East

articles.title: 🇸🇦 Saudi Pipeline Disruption Threatens Global Oil Supply
articles.description: Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline remains affected following drone attacks.
articles.content: The pipeline normally provides Saudi Arabia with an alternative route for transporting crude towards the Red Sea without depending entirely on the Strait of Hormuz. Reuters reports that the disruption could threaten as much as 4% of global oil supply if the pipeline remains offline. Saudi Arabia has limited stockpiles available while repairs and security assessments continue.
articles.imageQuery: Saudi Arabia East West oil pipeline

articles.title: 🇾🇪 Houthi Advance Raises Red Sea Shipping Concerns
articles.description: Iran-aligned Houthi forces have strengthened their position around Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
articles.content: The Houthi advance has created a second major maritime security concern alongside the Strait of Hormuz. Bab el-Mandeb connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and is an important route for international trade and energy shipments. Further disruption could increase shipping costs, insurance premiums and delivery times.
articles.imageQuery: Bab el Mandeb Yemen Red Sea shipping

articles.title: 🇮🇷 Iran Responsibility Claims Remain Disputed
articles.description: President Donald Trump has blamed Iran for the Saudi pipeline attack, but the allegation remains unconfirmed.
articles.content: Trump has said Iran was probably responsible for the attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline. Saudi and Iraqi authorities have reported that the drones originated from Iraqi territory, while an investigation continues. Iran and Iran-aligned groups have disputed responsibility for various attacks. RadiantWaves Media continues to distinguish confirmed facts from allegations.
articles.imageQuery: Donald Trump Iran Saudi Arabia Middle East

articles.title: 🇸🇪 Sweden Election Produces Extremely Close Result
articles.description: Sweden's centre-left opposition bloc holds a narrow lead over the governing right-wing bloc after Sunday's parliamentary election.
articles.content: Early results indicate a very close contest. The centre-left bloc led by Social Democrat Magdalena Andersson is currently projected to hold 175 seats in the 349-seat parliament, compared with 174 for the right-wing bloc. The final outcome is not yet fully settled because counting continues, including remaining votes from overseas and other ballots. The result could determine Sweden's future direction on immigration, public services and economic policy, as well as the role of the Sweden Democrats in government.

articles.title: 🇺🇦 Ukraine War Remains a Major European Security Concern
articles.description: The Russia-Ukraine war continues to influence European security, energy policy and defence planning.
articles.content: Ukraine continues to target Russian energy infrastructure while Russia maintains attacks on Ukrainian territory. European governments are closely monitoring the conflict as the wider Middle East crisis places additional pressure on Western military resources and energy markets.

articles.title: 🇨🇦🇪🇺 Canada Explores Closer Relationship With Europe
articles.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is reportedly considering a closer relationship between Canada and the European Union.
articles.content: The proposal could involve a new form of cooperation beyond Canada's existing relationship with the EU. Discussions reflect growing interest in strengthening economic, trade and security ties between Canada and Europe at a time of increasing geopolitical uncertainty.
articles.imageQuery: Canada European Union flags Mark Carney

articles.title: 🇳🇬 Dangote Refinery IPO Opens in Nigeria
articles.description: Dangote Refinery is moving ahead with what is expected to become Africa's largest-ever share offering.
articles.content: Nigeria's Securities and Exchange Commission has approved the Dangote Refinery IPO. The offer is expected to raise around $1.6 billion if fully subscribed. The company is also planning a $14.3 billion expansion that would increase processing capacity from 700,000 barrels per day to approximately 1.4 million barrels per day by 2029. The expansion could strengthen Nigeria's refining capacity and reduce dependence on imported petroleum products.

articles.title: 🇨🇩 DR Congo Continues Ebola Response
articles.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo continues its response to a major Ebola outbreak.
articles.content: Health authorities and international partners remain focused on surveillance, treatment and infection prevention. Previous government figures put confirmed cases above 7,000 and deaths above 3,000. The outbreak has spread across several provinces, making continued public-health measures essential.
articles.imageQuery: DR Congo Ebola health workers outbreak

articles.title: 🇺🇬 Uganda Continues Royal Succession Process
articles.description: Uganda continues discussions over the succession following the death and burial of King Oyo Nyimba of Toro.
articles.content: The late King Oyo Nyimba, who became monarch as a child and was once described as the world's youngest king, died at the age of 34. His succession has generated disagreement within the royal family and traditional leadership. The process remains closely watched in the Toro Kingdom.
articles.imageQuery: Uganda Toro Kingdom King Oyo Nyimba

articles.title: 📈 Global Markets Start Week Under Pressure
articles.description: Investors are watching oil prices, interest rates and geopolitical risks as markets begin a new week.
articles.content: The continuing Middle East crisis has pushed oil prices higher and increased concerns about inflation. Investors are also watching upcoming decisions from the US Federal Reserve and Bank of Japan. Higher energy prices could make it harder for central banks to reduce inflation without weakening economic growth.
articles.imageQuery: global stock market trading oil prices

articles.title: 🚗 Electric Vehicle Sales Continue to Expand
articles.description: Global electric-vehicle sales have continued to grow, although regional performance remains uneven.
articles.content: Europe remains an important growth market for electric vehicles, while China and North America have shown more mixed results. The continued expansion of EV sales is reshaping the global automobile industry and increasing competition between established manufacturers and newer electric-vehicle companies.

articles.title: 🤖 AI Safety Remains a Global Debate
articles.description: Governments and technology companies continue debating how increasingly capable artificial-intelligence systems should be developed and regulated.
articles.content: The rapid development of artificial intelligence has increased concerns about safety, privacy, employment and the possibility of increasingly autonomous systems. Governments are considering new rules while technology companies continue developing more powerful AI models. The central challenge is balancing innovation with appropriate safeguards.

articles.title: 🌏 Asian Markets React to Rising Oil Prices
articles.description: Asian financial markets are closely watching the energy crisis as higher oil prices increase inflation concerns.
articles.content: Countries that depend heavily on imported energy could face increased fuel and transportation costs if the Middle East disruption continues. Investors are also monitoring currency movements and upcoming monetary-policy decisions across the region.

morningSummary: Good morning. Global markets are beginning the week under pressure as the Middle East crisis pushes oil prices higher. Brent crude has risen above $107 a barrel after fresh attacks around Saudi Arabia and the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline remains disrupted, while Houthi forces in Yemen are increasing pressure around the Bab el-Mandeb shipping route. In Europe, Sweden's parliamentary election has produced an extremely close early result, with the centre-left opposition bloc narrowly ahead. Ukraine remains a major European security concern, while Canada is exploring closer cooperation with the European Union. In Nigeria, Dangote Refinery's landmark IPO opens today as the company moves ahead with a planned $14.3 billion expansion. Meanwhile, DR Congo continues its response to the Ebola outbreak and global technology companies face growing pressure over AI safety.
bigQuestion: With energy prices rising and major shipping routes under pressure, how long can the global economy absorb the consequences of prolonged disruption in the Middle East?
